prompt:
Edit the supplied Korean building artwork into a NEW companion UPGRADE SPRITE SHEET, matching the already approved game art. Reference image 1 (tower-tiers-v2.webp) is the approved style/camera/lighting/small-scale sprite treatment. Reference image 2 (buildings.webp) supplies the FOUR landmark identities described below. Output a precise FIVE COLUMNS by FOUR ROWS atlas, 20 equal SQUARE cells, 5:4 landscape sheet, real alpha transparent background, ONE complete isolated building in every cell.

Art direction: beautifully painted premium animated-film Korean historical fantasy game art, softly sculpted weathered granite, richly carved dark wood, elegant blue-black curved Korean tiles, deep-red lacquer posts, restrained muted green dancheong, antique gold trim, warm amber windows. Same elevated three-quarter ORTHOGRAPHIC game camera in all cells, looking down 45 degrees; warm upper-left key and cool blue fill. Same style as reference image 1, not more realistic or flatter. No people, text, numbers, UI, frame, gridline, watermark, environment, cast shadow puddles, noisy grit, hard black outlines, simple low-poly shapes or neon.

Exact grid is essential: FIVE equal columns, FOUR equal rows. Keep each complete object inside the CENTRAL 76% of its own square cell, leaving 12% truly transparent margin all around. Do not cross cell edges. All five versions in EACH row MUST have IDENTICAL compact ground footprint, total visible height and baseline; every upgrade modifies detail, material, inset architecture or equipment WITHIN the existing silhouette. Do NOT add another storey, expand the terrace, widen the base or enlarge the later columns. Final specializations are distinct shapes and equipment, not just a color change. First three tiers should be legibly different as SMALL gameplay sprites.

Columns LEFT TO RIGHT are: tier 1 modest original, tier 2 reinforced, tier 3 completed richly finished, MAX A unique specialization, MAX B another unique specialization. Never print these labels.

ROW 1 — GYEONGBOKGUNG Korean royal palace (reference image 2 row2 col3): one double-eaved royal hall with broad tiled roof, red pillars, carved lattice windows, compact raised stone terrace and central stair.
1 simple dark red timber royal hall, dark window lattice, plain stone terrace.
2 reinforced pale granite stair and railing posts, warm gold windows and two compact hanging lanterns, red-green carved roof brackets.
3 elaborate royal dancheong beams and bronze ridge ornaments, detailed finished stone balustrade with tiny carved guardians tucked inside original terrace, grand amber-lit central door, same two roofs.
4 ROYAL GOVERNANCE specialization: deep red drapes framing the central door, ornate antique gold royal sun emblem above entry, compact carved dragon ornaments and warm gold roof-end details, all within same hall outline.
5 ROYAL TREASURY specialization: central entry opened to visible stacked lacquer and bronze treasure chests, engraved jade/gold treasury doors, dark navy banners tucked under eaves and green-bronze roof ornaments, same footprint.

ROW 2 — NAMHANSANSEONG defensive watchtower (reference row2 col4): compact round granite bastion with crenellated parapet and a small dark tiled timber guard pavilion inside, restrained two pennants.
1 rough grey stone bastion, simple timber single roof pavilion, plain red pennants.
2 reinforced buttressed masonry and neatly dressed parapet, bronze-banded entry, amber guard lamp, stronger deep-red pennants, no footprint change.
3 finished darker dressed granite and carved guardhouse brackets, plated parapet trim and one recognizable royal guard shield mounted on front, completed navy-red pennants.
4 ELITE GARRISON specialization: compact heavy bronze shield plates on front parapet and two short spear bundles inside the bastion, red-and-gold elite standards, armored dark stone silhouette, same roof size.
5 WARRIOR MONKS specialization: two pale jade cloth prayer streamers, small carved lotus crest at guardhouse entry and paired compact stone lanterns integrated into parapet, jade-green and bronze details; no people.

ROW 3 — SEOKBINGGO Korean stone ice storehouse (reference row3 col1): a compact rounded grass-and-stone earth-covered vault, clearly visible small arched blue-lit entry with square ice blocks inside. NOT a snowy mountain or winter-only environment.
1 simple mossy stone vault and plain grey arch, a few blue ice blocks and tiny cool doorway light.
2 dressed arch blocks and stronger stone retaining bands, bronze-banded inset door frame, larger clearly defined pale blue ice slabs INSIDE the entry, compact side vents.
3 finished carved grey granite entrance with an etched snowflake-like bronze rosette above door, bright translucent layered ice stock within, neat mossy grass on vault and two compact stone vent caps.
4 COLD FRONT specialization: frosted pale-blue arch border and a large fan of jagged blue ice crystals inside the entry, a silver-blue vent at the top of the existing vault, subtle cool mist confined to doorway.
5 ICE PRISON specialization: a visible vertical barred gate made of translucent cyan ice inside the arch, compact dark-bronze side clamps and a tall inset hexagonal ice crystal core behind the gate; subtle jade ice glow, same vault shape.

ROW 4 — BULGUKSA stone pagoda complex (reference row3 col2 adapted to tower identity): a compact ornate Korean Dabotap-style pale granite pagoda, recognizable stacked stone platforms, delicate stone railings and central column, small amber shrine opening at center; no broad palace hall obscuring pagoda.
1 plain weathered granite pagoda on small square base, simple capstone, restrained amber shrine light.
2 restored pale granite railings and bracket stones, carved lotus footings, small bronze central shrine fittings, SAME total height and base.
3 beautifully finished intricately carved Dabotap stone tiers and lotus details, subtle antique-gold finial and two tiny warm inset lamps, same compact silhouette.
4 SEOKGATAP specialization: simpler elegant THREE-TIER Korean stone pagoda with broad clean square stone eaves, softly luminous gold central core and bronze lotus tip; redesign within the SAME height and footprint as the Dabotap.
5 LOTUS LANTERN specialization: retain ornate Dabotap silhouette and hang THREE clearly separate small jade-and-amber lotus lanterns from its middle stone railing, antique-gold chains and warm centered light, no huge exterior glow.

Spring/summer-compatible clean assets, no surrounding snow or terrain patches. Transparent pixels around each entire object. Excellent crisp reusable alpha silhouettes with painterly depth, readable at tiny battlefield size.
